Both answers are correct and O(m+n) in time. Assistant A uses a two-pointer scan with early termination and O(1) extra space. Assistant B builds the full merged list, which costs O(m+n) extra space and always processes every element, even though only the first k are needed.

A is the more efficient and elegant solution. It stops as soon as the kth element is found, and it handles an out-of-range k by returning None. B would raise an IndexError for k > m+n, and for k < 1 it would return a wrong element (k=0 gives merged_list[-1], the last element).

A's explanation is a bit inaccurate in one place, saying "it increments the pointer i" without mentioning the counting, but this is minor. Overall, A is better.

[[A]]
